```{r scratch-viz-setup, include=FALSE}
# Publication figure system: house theme, validated colour-vision-safe palette,
# and vector (PDF) output alongside every raster figure. Applied globally, so
# the plotting code below needs no changes. Guarded: if the library is not
# staged, the notebook renders exactly as it did before.
local({
  roots <- c(".", "assets/viz", Sys.getenv("SCRATCH_VIZ_DIR", "."))
  for (lib in c("scratch_viz.R", "scratch_report.R")) {
    for (r in roots) {
      p <- file.path(r, lib)
      if (file.exists(p)) { source(p, local = FALSE); break }
    }
  }
})
```

## Loading library

```{r library, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, echo = TRUE}

#| code-fold: true

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(DT)

```

## Report interactive table

```{r merging_report, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
#| code-fold: true

metric_report_db <- data.frame()

for (sample_metric in input_metrics_report) {
  metric_report_tmp <- read_csv(file = sample_metric)
  metric_report_db <- rbind(
        metric_report_db,
        metric_report_tmp
    )

}

```

```{r}
#| column: screen-inset-shaded

# scratch_table(), not DT::datatable() directly: it renders the same searchable
# table AND registers it, which is what puts the numbers in front of the in-page
# agent. A raw DT call is invisible to the agent, so this report could be
# summarised but not queried — the cohort metrics table is the one thing a reader
# is most likely to ask about.
scratch_table(metric_report_db, caption = "Per-sample cohort metrics", page = 15)

```

## Cohort QC summary {#cohort-summary}

```{r cohort-compute, include = FALSE}
# This report previously rendered one interactive table and drew no conclusion
# from it. It is the ONLY place that sees every sample at once, so it is the
# only place that can say which samples are outliers, whether sequencing was
# deep enough, and which filter is actually removing cells.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(data.table); library(ggplot2)})
.m <- as.data.table(metric_report_db)
.num <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
for (cc in setdiff(names(.m), c("sample_id", "status_flag")))
  if (!is.numeric(.m[[cc]])) .m[[cc]] <- .num(.m[[cc]])
.has <- function(x) x %in% names(.m)
.n_samp <- nrow(.m)

# Outliers judged against the OTHER samples, not an absolute cutoff: what counts
# as shallow depends on the assay and the cohort.
.flag_outlier <- function(v) {
  if (length(v) < 3 || all(is.na(v))) return(rep(FALSE, length(v)))
  md <- median(v, na.rm = TRUE); dv <- mad(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(dv) || dv == 0) return(rep(FALSE, length(v)))
  abs(v - md) > 3 * dv
}
```

```{r cohort-findings, results = 'asis'}
.failed <- if (.has("status_flag")) .m[!grepl("SUCCESS", status_flag)]$sample_id else character(0)
.tot <- if (.has("n_observed_cells")) sum(.m$n_observed_cells, na.rm = TRUE) else NA

msg <- sprintf("**%d sample%s** processed%s.", .n_samp, ifelse(.n_samp == 1, "", "s"),
               if (!is.na(.tot)) sprintf(", yielding **%s cells** after QC",
                                         format(.tot, big.mark = ",")) else "")
# Braced deliberately: at top level R terminates `if (cond) expr` at the
# newline and then fails on a bare `else`. (Inside {} it would parse fine.)
if (length(.failed)) {
  msg <- paste(msg, sprintf(
    "**Sample(s) %s did not pass** and are excluded from everything downstream.",
    paste(.failed, collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  msg <- paste(msg, "All samples passed the QC gate.")
}
scratch_finding(msg, type = if (length(.failed)) "caution" else "note",
                title = "Cohort status")

# --- which filter is doing the work -----------------------------------------
if (all(c("n_total_cells","n_thr_features_cells","n_observed_cells") %in% names(.m))) {
  .lost_gene <- sum(.m$n_total_cells - .m$n_thr_features_cells, na.rm = TRUE)
  .lost_mito <- sum(.m$n_thr_features_cells - .m$n_observed_cells, na.rm = TRUE)
  .lost_all  <- .lost_gene + .lost_mito
  .kept <- 100 * sum(.m$n_observed_cells, na.rm = TRUE) / max(1, sum(.m$n_total_cells, na.rm = TRUE))
  m2 <- sprintf(paste("Across the cohort **%.1f%%** of barcodes were retained.",
                      "Of the **%s** cells removed, **%s (%.0f%%)** went to the gene-count",
                      "filter and **%s (%.0f%%)** to the mitochondrial filter."),
                .kept, format(.lost_all, big.mark = ","),
                format(.lost_gene, big.mark = ","), 100 * .lost_gene / max(1, .lost_all),
                format(.lost_mito, big.mark = ","), 100 * .lost_mito / max(1, .lost_all))
  if (.lost_gene == 0) m2 <- paste(m2,
    "**The gene-count filter removed nothing**, so it is not currently constraining this",
    "cohort -- every cell lost was lost to mitochondrial content. Tightening the gene",
    "threshold would have no effect; the mitochondrial cutoff is the one that matters here.")
  if (.lost_mito == 0) m2 <- paste(m2,
    "**The mitochondrial filter removed nothing** -- worth confirming the `MT-` gene",
    "prefix matches this reference, since a prefix mismatch produces exactly this result.")
  scratch_finding(m2, type = "note", title = "Which filter is removing cells")
}

# --- sequencing depth / saturation ------------------------------------------
if (.has("seq_saturation")) {
  .st <- .m$seq_saturation[is.finite(.m$seq_saturation)]
  if (length(.st)) {
    .low <- .m[is.finite(seq_saturation) & seq_saturation < 50]$sample_id
    m3 <- sprintf("Sequencing saturation ranges **%.1f%% to %.1f%%** (median %.1f%%).",
                  min(.st), max(.st), median(.st))
    if (length(.low)) m3 <- paste(m3, sprintf(paste(
      "**Sample(s) %s are below 50%%**, meaning a substantial fraction of transcripts",
      "remain unsampled -- deeper sequencing would still recover new genes, and these",
      "samples will show artificially low gene counts relative to the rest."),
      paste(.low, collapse = ", ")))
    else m3 <- paste(m3, "All samples are adequately saturated, so gene-count differences",
                     "between them reflect biology rather than sequencing depth.")
    scratch_finding(m3, type = if (length(.low)) "caution" else "note",
                    title = "Sequencing saturation")
  }
}

# --- per-metric outliers -----------------------------------------------------
.checkcols <- intersect(c("median_genes_per_cell","median_umi_per_cell",
                          "mean_reads_per_cell","seq_saturation","n_observed_cells"),
                        names(.m))
if (.n_samp >= 3 && length(.checkcols)) {
  .out <- rbindlist(lapply(.checkcols, function(cc) {
    f <- .flag_outlier(.m[[cc]])
    if (!any(f)) return(NULL)
    data.table(metric = cc, sample = .m$sample_id[f], value = .m[[cc]][f],
               cohort_median = median(.m[[cc]], na.rm = TRUE))
  }))
  if (length(.out) && nrow(.out)) {
    scratch_finding(sprintf(paste("**%d sample-metric combination(s)** sit more than 3 MADs",
                                  "from the cohort median (%s). These are the samples most",
                                  "likely to drive batch effects downstream."),
                            nrow(.out), paste(unique(.out$sample), collapse = ", ")),
                    type = "caution", title = "Outlying samples")
    scratch_table(.out, caption = "Metrics more than 3 MADs from the cohort median")
  } else {
    scratch_finding("No sample deviates more than 3 MADs from the cohort median on any QC metric.",
                    type = "note", title = "Outlying samples")
  }
} else if (.n_samp < 3) {
  scratch_finding(sprintf(paste("With only %d sample%s, outlier detection across samples is",
                                "not meaningful -- a median and MAD need at least three points."),
                          .n_samp, ifelse(.n_samp == 1, "", "s")),
                  type = "note", title = "Outlying samples")
}
```

```{r cohort-retention-figure, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
if (all(c("n_total_cells","n_thr_features_cells","n_observed_cells") %in% names(.m))) {
  .r <- rbindlist(list(
    .m[, .(sample_id, stage = "removed: low gene count",
           cells = n_total_cells - n_thr_features_cells)],
    .m[, .(sample_id, stage = "removed: high mitochondrial",
           cells = n_thr_features_cells - n_observed_cells)],
    .m[, .(sample_id, stage = "retained", cells = n_observed_cells)]))
  .r[, stage := factor(stage, levels = c("retained", "removed: low gene count",
                                         "removed: high mitochondrial"))]
  .r[, tip := sprintf("%s\n%s\n%s cells", sample_id, stage, format(cells, big.mark = ","))]
  ggplot(.r, aes(sample_id, cells, fill = stage, text = tip)) +
    geom_col(width = .7) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("retained" = "#0d366b",
                                 "removed: low gene count" = "#8fb4dd",
                                 "removed: high mitochondrial" = "#8c1d18"), name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .08))) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Barcode fate per sample",
         subtitle = "a tall red segment means the mitochondrial cutoff is doing the filtering",
         x = NULL, y = "barcodes") +
    theme_scratch()
}
```

```{r cohort-depth-figure, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 4.5
if (all(c("mean_reads_per_cell","median_genes_per_cell") %in% names(.m))) {
  .d <- copy(.m)
  .d[, tip := sprintf("%s\n%s reads/cell\n%s genes/cell%s", sample_id,
                      format(round(mean_reads_per_cell), big.mark = ","),
                      format(round(median_genes_per_cell), big.mark = ","),
                      if ("seq_saturation" %in% names(.d))
                        sprintf("\n%.1f%% saturation", seq_saturation) else "")]
  .aes <- if ("seq_saturation" %in% names(.d))
    aes(mean_reads_per_cell, median_genes_per_cell, colour = seq_saturation, text = tip)
  else aes(mean_reads_per_cell, median_genes_per_cell, text = tip)
  ggplot(.d, .aes) +
    geom_point(size = 3.2) +
    { if ("seq_saturation" %in% names(.d))
        scale_colour_gradient(low = "#8c1d18", high = "#0d366b", name = "saturation %") } +
    scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(title = "Sequencing depth against library complexity",
         subtitle = "a sample low and left is undersequenced; low and right is genuinely low-complexity",
         x = "mean reads per cell", y = "median genes per cell") +
    theme_scratch()
}
```
